title.value: A Reproducible and Realistic Evaluation of Partial Domain Adaptation Methods
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: A Reproducible and Realistic Evaluation of Partial Domain Adaptation Methods

extractions.description: The paper evaluates partial domain adaptation (PDA) methods, which aim to classify unlabeled target images using labeled source images, where the target domain classes are a subset of the source domain classes. The study focuses on the impact of model selection strategies on the performance of PDA methods, using multiple algorithms, datasets, and model selection strategies.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is about improving machine learning techniques for domain adaptation, not directly focused on sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) aims at classifying unlabeled target images leveraging source labeled ones. In this work, we consider the Partial Domain Adaptation (PDA) variant, where we have extra source classes not present in the target domain.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on machine learning methodology rather than a specific climate or ecologically-related sustainable development category.
primary_category.quote: The main goal of this work is to provide a realistic evaluation of PDA methods with the different model selection strategies under a consistent evaluation protocol.
